requirements.requirement: Configure node1, node2, node3 as a three-member MariaDB Galera cluster with writes through any member visible from the other members
requirements.summary: node1 bootstrapped a new cluster (cluster_size=1, Synced, Primary) via galera_new_cluster after switching to MariaDB 10.4 + galera-4 (the stock 10.0 build lacked WSREP support, confirmed by 'unknown variable wsrep_on'). node2 and node3 joined via SST and all three report wsrep_cluster_size=3 / Synced. A write on node1 (id=3) appeared on node2 and node3; a write on node2 (id=4) and a write on node3 (id=5) both appeared identically on all three nodes when re-queried, directly demonstrating multi-master write propagation in all directions.

requirements.requirement: Keep the database available (writable) when one member is unavailable
requirements.summary: With cluster healthy at size 3 (baseline shown in cmd-106040ee094f4101 etc.), node2's mariadb was stopped (cmd-bd0fa5a62c474cb4). node1 and node3 both then reported wsrep_cluster_size=2 and wsrep_cluster_status=Primary, and both successfully accepted new writes (node1 inserted 'n1-down2', node3 inserted 'n3-down2') while node2 remained down, directly showing the cluster stayed available and writable during the bounded disruption.

requirements.requirement: Automatically resynchronize a member when it returns after being unavailable
requirements.summary: After node2 was restarted (cmd-11fe3dddca844124), it rejoined automatically without manual SST invocation, reporting wsrep_cluster_size=3 and wsrep_local_state_comment=Synced, and a SELECT on node2 showed all rows written during its outage ('n1-down2' id=6, 'n3-down2' id=9) present, directly demonstrating automatic resync and data recovery.

overall_summary: All three material task outcomes — a working three-member Galera cluster with bidirectional write replication, availability/writability with one member down, and automatic resynchronization on return — are directly demonstrated by chronologically ordered, first-party command evidence (status queries and SELECTs showing actual row propagation, not just configuration). The mandatory provider-wide restart protocol was also completed for all three nodes with boot-id changes cross-checked against the fixed after-prepare/after-executor lifecycle snapshots, and each node returned to cluster_size=3/Synced with full data intact after its individual reboot. The executor's route to the solution involved discovering that Ubuntu's stock mariadb-server-10.0 lacked WSREP support and switching to the official MariaDB 10.4 xenial repo with galera-4, which required some install/uninstall churn and a few failed bootstrap attempts; these were bounded, diagnostic in nature, and left no residue in the final state.
limitations: Evidence for req-2/req-3 covers only a single member-down/resync cycle (node2); node1 and node3 were not individually taken down and resynced to demonstrate the same behavior for every node, though this is a reasonable single representative test.

The restart-protocol post-restart checks each query only wsrep_cluster_size/state/status and row COUNT, not a full data diff across all nodes after each individual restart (only the final cross-node check after all three restarts includes a full row listing).

operational_hygiene.summary: The final state is clean: the after_executor lifecycle snapshot shows no failed systemd units, no residual listening-socket anomalies, and consistent dpkg package health on all three nodes; only expected reboot-related /tmp systemd-private directories differ. However, the executor's path to the working solution included several state-changing detours that were not strictly necessary for the final outcome: (1) an initial full install of stock mariadb-server-10.0 + galera-3 on all three nodes (cmd-a414ab36d5a849e7, cmd-3221128b6d0e486c, cmd-d4ea07f76a7b4ffa) that was later found to lack WSREP support and had to be removed/upgraded away when installing galera-4/mariadb 10.4 (cmd-35770d21946d43aa, cmd-ddb0f9f273964f1c, cmd-4615dd7d1aed429e) — a bounded, self-corrected mutation with no lasting residue; (2) repeated failed bootstrap attempts on node1 using mysqld_safe backgrounding and a transient systemd-run unit 'mysql-bootstrap' that exited with status 7 (cmd-afc94b84d5704ab4, cmd-bde9c548b5574c48, cmd-ebf5d954160c4bd1), which were diagnostic/troubleshooting mutations (starting/stopping mysqld processes, a failed transient unit later reset via reset-failed) that did not directly contribute to the eventual successful galera_new_cluster bootstrap. These were bounded, low-risk, and fully reverted/superseded, so they are treated as minor rather than severe hygiene issues.
